mbm-1076.quote: My nephew marks each golf shot on a little map with his purple crayon. After my ball disappeared in the reeds he drew a sea monster there. I’ve played wide of that monster ever since.

mbm-1077.clue: I always check the tile at the threshold.
mbm-1077.quote: While sightseeing I found one green fish among a hundred plain entrance tiles. The shopkeeper told me her father had set it there. I bought a postcard and asked her to draw me a second fish.

mbm-1078.clue: Our bakery can count to seven under cover.
mbm-1078.quote: I quilted a cover for my brother's rising bread dough. It has seven red tabs along the edge. He flips one for every loaf he shapes, and on busy mornings asks if I can sew faster than he can bake.

mbm-1079.clue: I make room for the blue heron.
mbm-1079.quote: There’s a bend on our canoe route where a heron fishes from the same stump. I put the paddle down and let us drift past. Last week we both came home with an excellent view of breakfast.

mbm-1080.clue: My drafts keep a night shift.
mbm-1080.quote: I write one line before bed and leave a blank for morning. Last night’s line was about a foghorn. I woke to the milk truck and wrote that sound in instead. The harbor suddenly felt like home.

mbm-1081.clue: I have a song for the third-floor landing.
mbm-1081.quote: Our narrow stairwell rings on one particular note. I sing it softly on my way upstairs. Once a neighbor opened her door and sang the harmony she’d been practicing behind it.

mbm-1082.clue: I know where the animators hid the cat.
mbm-1082.quote: We counted the same little orange cat in four different station scenes at anime club. I made a paper ticket for it and pinned it beside our other drawings. It has traveled farther than any hero.

mbm-1083.clue: I packed a laugh in the prop trunk.
mbm-1083.quote: I made a fake cake for a comedy with an alarm clock inside. When our leading lady cut it the thing began to ring. I’ve never had a better review from the back row.

mbm-1084.clue: My assistant rolls in on three wheels.
mbm-1084.quote: I practice linking metal rings on the back porch. When one rolled downhill my little cousin fetched it on the handlebars of her tricycle. Now she wheels onstage whenever I announce my assistant.

mbm-1085.clue: My quilt has a place for a thumbnail.
mbm-1085.quote: Dad drew me a winding road for a patchwork map. I stitched a narrow garage at one end so my nephew could park his thumbnail there and drive it through the hills before bed.

mbm-1086.clue: I wore my brother’s lucky stripes.
mbm-1086.quote: I skied the first run in his hand-me-down striped scarf, tucked snug inside my jacket. At the lift he spotted one tiny green stripe at my neck from across the queue. He still thinks it steered me.

mbm-1087.clue: I carried home one half of a bookend.
mbm-1087.quote: The market stall had a carved wooden elephant looking sideways at nobody. I put him beside my books and made a little paper elephant to look back. The two sizes make a better pair.

mbm-1088.clue: I give the king a wooden spoon.
mbm-1088.quote: Our glove-puppet king lost his scepter during rehearsal. I used a tiny stirring spoon instead. The children requested soup at every royal audience, so we had to add a palace cook.

mbm-1089.clue: I read the dedication a second time.
mbm-1089.quote: A secondhand book was dedicated to someone with my mother’s name. I gave it to her and she wrote me a new dedication on a slip of paper. I’ve kept both together.

mbm-1090.clue: I keep my ball out of the moat.
mbm-1090.quote: Our mini-golf castle has a real puddle where the painted moat cracked. A sparrow used it as a bath while I lined up my putt. I played around the castle to give it room.

mbm-1091.clue: I stitched the kitchen radio in blue.
mbm-1091.quote: Our family quilt shows each of us a little differently. Dad is the radio on the sill because he always cooks with music. The blue dial comes from the shirt he wore on Sundays.

mbm-1092.clue: That white mark is all mine.
mbm-1092.quote: There’s a scuff on the bowling approach shaped like a crescent moon. My coach told me to start two shoes behind it. Years later I can still find my starting spot when they dim the lights.

mbm-1093.clue: I taped the rehearsal to my bicycle.
mbm-1093.quote: I used a cassette player in the front basket to practice a son chorus as I pedaled home. At every red light I sang the next line. The fruit seller learned it before I did.

mbm-1094.clue: I’ve got a leather moon on my wrist.
mbm-1094.quote: I stamped a little crescent into my watch strap for each night shift my sister worked while studying. When she graduated the strap was full. I made her the matching one with a single bright sun.

mbm-1095.clue: I watch the paddle tip for the first red leaf.
mbm-1095.quote: I canoe the same little channel all year. In autumn the first red leaf always sticks to my paddle for a moment. I press that one in my calendar before the rest of the river changes.

mbm-1096.clue: I keep a flower for the bandleader.
mbm-1096.quote: At our ballroom social I pin a paper carnation on the bandstand before the first dance. By the last waltz the trumpet player has it tucked in his hat. We both consider that good manners.

mbm-1097.clue: I use my quilt as a calendar.
mbm-1097.quote: I stitch one small colored patch after the first frost each year. The oldest patch came from the coat I wore to school. I can find it with my fingers in the dark.

mbm-1098.clue: I dry the leather over a wooden peach.
mbm-1098.quote: I molded a little coin purse around a piece of turned wood from my granddad’s shop. It opens along the peach’s seam. The first coin I put inside bought the thread for its leaf.

mbm-1099.clue: I can hear the harmony in our mixing bowls.
mbm-1099.quote: My sister and I sing while drying the dishes. Hold the big steel bowl just right and it sends her low note singing back at me. We always leave that bowl until last.

mbm-1100.clue: I made the bakery a bell.
mbm-1100.quote: I shaped a little clay croissant with a hollow belly and a clay bead inside. Now the bakery door jingles softly when I walk in for my Saturday roll. The baker says it asks for butter.
